name: Socialstyrelsen: Min insats (National Board of Health and Welfare: information on fostering and other volunteer roles)
notes: Information only. It tells people to contact their own municipality, or any other, and its Register your interest page lists every municipality by name. Its fostering page (updated 20 June 2024) still says many municipalities use Familjehem Sverige, which has closed (next row). It explains the family home investigation (familjehemsutredning), the training and the payment, and has films and a webinar.

name: Familjehem Sverige (familjehemsverige.se; former national enquiry service built by SKR, the Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Regions)
coverage: Sweden (it served the municipalities that joined it)
notes: Closed. The page now says the service has been wound up (avvecklats) and tells people to contact their municipality. SKR's 2020 material (search result) describes a self-test and an interest form whose answers went to the municipality. Socialstyrelsen's Min insats pages and some council pages, such as Örnsköldsvik's, still point to it. SKR is the members' organisation of Sweden's municipalities and regions, so local_authority is the closest operator type.

name: Myndigheten för familjerätt och föräldraskapsstöd (MFoF, Family Law and Parental Support Authority): intercountry adoption
coverage: Sweden (central authority for intercountry adoption; office in Skellefteå)
notes: Information only: people apply first to the social services in their own municipality. MFoF authorises and supervises adoption organisations, coordinates the compulsory parent education before adoption and decides whether an adoption without an organisation (enskild adoption) may go ahead. The brief named a family law department at Socialstyrelsen; the pages read on 28 November 2026 show MFoF still doing this work under its own name, and the Act on intercountry adoption mediation still names it. Whether the former MIA's work moved here is unverified. An MFoF answer of 5 May 2026 says the government has not yet set a timetable for a possible ban on intercountry adoption mediation.

name: Adoptionscentrum (AC; authorised adoption organisation)
notes: Its own site showed our reader an automated browser check instead of content, so we did not read it. MFoF's page (updated 10 September 2026) lists a phone line and an email address for it. It says AC is the only organisation still mediating intercountry adoptions, with authorisation in Sweden until 31 December 2030, for Colombia, India, Serbia, South Africa, Taiwan and Thailand. MFoF's 2025 supervision report (search result) says AC mediated 35 adoptions in 2025. Founded in 1969; its legal form was not checked.

name: Barnen Framför Allt – Adoptioner (BFA, Children Above All – Adoptions)
notes: Winding down since September 2024 and takes no new applicants (MFoF page, updated 10 September 2026). Its authorisation runs to 31 December 2027 so it can finish open cases, for India and Taiwan. Its records are now held by MFoF. The old address bfa.se now leads to an unrelated gambling site, so we give no website.

name: Humana Familjehemsvård (Humana: consultant-supported foster care)
coverage: Sweden (national provider; also family homes for adults and treatment foster care, TFCO)
notes: Consultant-supported foster care (konsulentstödd familjehemsvård): municipalities buy placements and Humana's consultants support the family. The pages give a national email address and phone line; we found an interest form only for family homes for adults. Criteria: a spare room, a room of their own for every child in the home, and own children older than 3. Its FAQ says there is no upper age limit. The assessment has two or three home visits, references, register checks and an in-depth interview. A consultant is available in the day and an on-call line at other times.

name: Skyddsvärnet – anno 1910: jour- och familjehemsvård (emergency and foster care)
coverage: Sweden (all ages; regional contacts in Stockholm, Sundsvall, Linköping, Göteborg, Kristianstad and Helsingborg)
notes: Non-profit social care organisation founded in 1910 (its legal form was not checked). It offers emergency and foster care across Sweden and takes all kinds of placements, working with trained carers. The page lists named staff with direct phone numbers and emails, which we do not record. We found no enquiry form or criteria for new carers. Page dated 17 November 2026.

name: Stockholms stad: Familjehem och jourhem (City of Stockholm: foster and emergency care)
coverage: City of Stockholm (the social services administration, Socialförvaltningen)
notes: The interest form is a survey on a third-party survey service (esMaker), whose robots.txt refused our reader, so we did not read the questions. After an enquiry the city makes a first assessment: conversations, register checks with the police, social services, the Enforcement Authority (Kronofogden) and the Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan), and a digital information film. A fuller investigation with home visits comes before a child moves in. Criteria: over 25, stable finances, an occupation, good Swedish, good health, a support network, experience of children, no child under 3 at home and a room for the child. Monthly digital information meetings. Page updated 20 October 2026. An SVT news report says the city gets about 500 enquiries a year (search result).

name: Stockholms stad: Adoption (City of Stockholm: adoption)
coverage: City of Stockholm (the district committees, stadsdelsnämnder)
notes: Says an adopter must be 18 or over and can be married, a registered partner, cohabiting or single. Intercountry adoption, and adoption of a known child from abroad (enskild adoption), both need consent (medgivande) from the district committee; enskild adoption also needs a permit from MFoF. Adoption within Sweden is applied for at the district court. In every municipality, social services carry out this home study (medgivandeutredning) for the people who live there.

name: Huddinge kommun: Familjehem (Huddinge Municipality: foster care)
notes: People contact the family home unit (familjehemsenheten). The page lists recruiters by name with direct phone numbers and emails, which we do not record. An information meeting was listed for 18 November 2026. Approval needs a family home investigation with several home visits, interviews and checks in public registers. Carers get external supervision, support and training. Page updated 5 October 2026.

name: Nacka kommun: Bli familjehem (Nacka Municipality: become a foster carer)
notes: Interest is registered through an e-service, and the page links to a PDF guide on how to use it; we did not read the e-service. Everything is summed up in a written investigation for the social committee's decision. Payment is based on the child's age and needs, with SKR's recommendations as the guide.

name: Södertälje kommun: Familjehem och jourhem (Södertälje Municipality: foster and emergency care)
notes: Interest through an e-service (not read). Digital information meetings: the service sends a link after sign-up. Carers need a free room, time, patience and commitment, and must be able to take time off work for daytime meetings with social services, health care and school. They are expected to take part in the training and supervision offered.

name: Stockholms Stadsmission: familjehem och jourhem (Stockholm City Mission: foster and emergency care)
coverage: Stockholm area (the page covers young people and adults)
notes: The page refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on a search result. It describes an interest form, then a longer questionnaire, an interview and a written assessment. Non-profit city mission.

name: Patia: Bli familjehem (Patia AB: consultant-supported foster care)
coverage: Stockholm area (office in Solna; it says it has framework agreements with over 150 municipalities)
notes: The Become a foster carer link opens an email to the agency, and the page gives a phone line. It promises consultant support around the clock, training and supervision, and payment in line with the usual recommendations.

name: NEB-teamet: Familjehem Stockholm (consultant-supported foster care)
coverage: Stockholm and around it, from Norrköping or Linköping in the south to Gävle in the north (the page names both)
notes: The interest link opens a posting on a job recruitment platform (Teamtailor), not a form on its own site; we did not read it. Carers get their own consultant, staff available around the clock, external supervision, training, carer meetings and respite. All carers take the Ett hem att växa i course. Page dated 1 October 2025.

name: Uppsala kommun: Bli familjehem eller jourhem (Uppsala Municipality: placement unit, Placeringsenheten)
notes: The e-service needs a BankID or Freja eID login, so we did not read it. Uppsala asks applicants to be ideally 25 to 65, live within driving distance, have no child aged 3 or under, give the child a room without anyone giving up theirs, and have stable housing, health, income and good Swedish. It lists eight steps: a first assessment and call, register checks, an office meeting with questionnaires, a home visit and interview, extra information, a place in a matching bank, a call about a child, then the full family home and matching investigation. All carers take Ett hem att växa i.

name: Eskilstuna kommun: Vi söker fler familjehem (Eskilstuna Municipality: family home unit)
notes: The family home unit answers questions and handles interest registrations by phone and email; we found no web form. The investigation includes home visits, interviews, register checks and references. Eskilstuna follows SKR's payment recommendations. Page updated 16 October 2026.

name: Nyköpings kommun: Familjehem och jourhem (Nyköping Municipality: foster and emergency care)
notes: The page has a short contact form: name, email and a message. The unit then calls for a first conversation. New carers take Ett hem att växa i, run by the family home unit, and the social committee then gives its consent. The page says the committee considers moving custody after three years in the same home; the 2025 Social Services Act says two years.

name: Startsteget: Familjehem (Startsteget AB: consultant-supported foster care)
coverage: Sweden (based in Eskilstuna; the page read is its Stockholm page)
notes: The page has its own interest form. It asks for name, year of birth, address, phone, email, relationship status, children at home and type of home. It also asks about experience of neuropsychiatric disability, substance misuse and self-harm, how well the person speaks Swedish, and whether anyone is on police, social insurance, debt or social services registers, and lets people upload an earlier assessment. The company says it holds a permit from IVO, the Health and Social Care Inspectorate, for foster care. It says there is no age limit, but carers should be able to be there until the young person is past 20.

name: Linköpings kommun: Bli familjehem (Linköping Municipality: become a foster carer)
notes: One e-service takes interest in several roles: emergency home, foster home, contact family, contact person and summer family; we did not read it. A social worker then calls, and the investigation uses interviews, home visits and references. Linköping looks for a safe and stable life, good health, time, a room for the child, stable finances and knowledge of Swedish. New carers take a basic course of eight sessions before they start. Payment follows SKR. Regular information meetings. Page updated 15 September 2026.

name: Norrköpings kommun: Bli uppdragstagare (Norrköping Municipality: become a carer or volunteer)
notes: People are invited to an information meeting first, online or in person; dates were listed from December 2026 to June 2027, and the sign-up asks for name, email and phone. The interest form needs BankID, so we did not read it; the page says it asks for personal details, the role and why, and about the family. A short phone interview follows, then a decision on whether to investigate. Checks cover the police, Kronofogden, the register of people taken into custody for drunkenness (LOB), Försäkringskassan and social services.

name: Familjehemsresursen (joint foster carer recruitment for the municipalities in Jönköping County)
coverage: Municipalities in Jönköping County (through Kommunal utveckling at Region Jönköpings län)
notes: Search results only. Region Jönköpings län papers describe a county-wide recruitment resource staffed since 2012, and the 2025 annual report lists it among the joint areas run by Kommunal utveckling. We found no public enquiry page. jonkoping.se/familjehem returned 'not found' to our reader, so Jönköping Municipality's own route was not checked.

name: Ljungby kommun: Familjehem (Ljungby Municipality: foster care)
notes: Interest through an e-service (not read). Approval follows a structured interview, register extracts and references. Växjö's fostering page was not found by our reader; search results say Växjö's family home unit also serves Lessebo, Tingsryd and Uppvidinge (unverified).

name: Kalmar kommun: Vill du hjälpa ett barn (Kalmar Municipality: family home unit)
notes: One e-service takes interest in foster home, emergency home, contact family and contact person roles. Its steps are details, preview and send, and the start page does not say a login is needed; we did not open the form. The family home unit then gets in touch. Kalmar Municipality is also one of the providers of parent education before intercountry adoption listed by MFoF.

name: Region Gotland: Familjehem, kontaktfamilj och kontaktperson (foster care, contact families and contact persons)
coverage: Gotland (Region Gotland also acts as the municipality)
notes: E-service for foster home, emergency home, contact family and contact person roles (not opened); its start page says it collects the personal identity number. The family home unit then calls. Register extracts from the police, social services, Kronofogden and Försäkringskassan come before the investigation starts. Payment follows SKR. Page updated 15 November 2026.

name: Ronneby kommun: Intresseanmälan kontaktfamilj/familjehem (Ronneby Municipality: interest in contact family or foster care)
notes: E-service for contact family, foster home and emergency home interest (not read). The service then gets in touch. Karlskrona's site showed our reader an automated browser check, so Blekinge's largest municipality has no row yet.

name: Malmö stad: Bli familjehem (City of Malmö: foster care recruitment team, Familjehemsvårdens rekryteringsteam)
notes: The e-service needs BankID or Freja eID+; its steps are role, housing, personal details, personal information, other information, preview and send. People with protected identity are asked to phone instead. It says the investigation will ask Försäkringskassan, social services, the police (suspicion and criminal records registers), Kronofogden and the LOB register. Malmö's FAQ says the child needs their own room in most cases, carers need an occupation, and age does not decide. Support includes an evening and weekend helpline. Fostering page updated 23 October 2026.

name: Helsingborgs stad: Ansök om att bli familjehem (City of Helsingborg: family home unit)
notes: No login needed. The form asks for first name, surname, role (foster home, contact person or family, specially appointed guardian, emergency home), street address, postcode, town, day and evening phone, email, family type (married or cohabiting, or single), children at home aged 1 to 12 and 12 to 18, number of rooms, any earlier role and other information. A recruiter then calls; home visits and in-depth interviews follow, and the social committee decides. Form page updated 17 March 2025.

name: Lunds kommun: Vi behöver fler familjehem och jourhem (Lund Municipality: foster and emergency care)
notes: The e-service's robots.txt refused our reader. Lund asks for a free room, a room of their own for each child already at home, and fluent spoken and written Swedish for the adults. A first call follows the enquiry, and training follows approval. Payment follows SKR. Page updated 29 October 2026.

name: Kristianstads kommun: Familjehem, kontaktfamilj (Kristianstad Municipality: foster care team)
notes: E-service for foster home, contact family and emergency home interest (not read). Applicants can order their own social services register extract through another e-service with BankID. Checks cover Kronofogden, the police, Försäkringskassan, the Transport Agency (Transportstyrelsen) and social services. Contracted emergency homes need 1 to 3 free bedrooms, a carer at home full time, a driving licence and a car. Page updated 21 September 2026.

name: Halmstads kommun: Att vara familjehem eller jourhem (Halmstad Municipality: foster and emergency care)
notes: One e-service for interest in several roles: respite carer, companion, contact person, contact family, support family and foster home (not read). The fee depends on the child's needs and the carer's work, using SKR's guidelines. Fostering page updated 15 April 2026.

name: Göteborgs Stad: Familjehem (City of Gothenburg: foster care)
notes: No login needed. The form asks which roles interest the person (contact or support family, foster home, emergency home), any earlier role, family situation and housing (both required, in free text, including the number of bedrooms), name, address, postcode, town, email, mobile and how they heard of the service. Monthly information meetings. The page says the city most needs experienced families, in or outside Göteborg, for school-age children.

name: Borås Stad: Familjehemscentrum – Gör en insats (City of Borås: foster care centre)
stated_response_time: As soon as possible (så snart som möjligt)
notes: No login needed. The form asks for name, phone, email, which roles (foster home, emergency home, contact family, contact person, contact support, extra adult, specially appointed guardian or other) and any wishes. The centre covers several roles, including specially appointed guardian. Page changed 2 July 2026.

name: Trollhättans stad: Familjehem (City of Trollhättan: family home unit)
notes: We found no web form; people contact the unit by phone or email. Single people, same-sex couples, older and younger people and people of any culture are welcome, and carers can live outside Trollhättan. The child needs a room of their own. Checks cover social services, the police, Försäkringskassan, Transportstyrelsen and Kronofogden. The page gives typical payments: expenses from about SEK 5,000 (most carers get about SEK 7,000 to 8,000) and a fee usually between about SEK 11,500 and SEK 17,500 a month. The unit says it holds an LGBTQI+ certification.

name: Karlstads kommun: Familjehem, jourhem, kontaktfamilj och kontaktperson (Karlstad Municipality: family home unit)
notes: The e-service needs an e-ID; people without one are asked to phone the contact centre. We read only its start page. The family home unit also answers questions by email.

name: Örebro kommun: Familjehem och jourhem (Örebro Municipality: family home unit)
notes: We found no web form; people email the family home unit or phone the service centre. Örebro says carers should be at least 25 and able to make themselves understood in Swedish. The investigation usually takes several months, with meetings and home visits; training with other new carers follows. Payment follows SKR.

name: Västerås stad: Familjehem, kontaktfamilj, kontaktperson (City of Västerås: family home unit)
notes: The e-service goes straight to an e-ID login, so we did not read it. After an enquiry the unit gets in touch. Checks cover the police, the social services register, Försäkringskassan, Kronofogden and Transportstyrelsen. No special knowledge is needed. Reinforced foster homes and contracted emergency homes need earlier experience and a carer at home full time.

name: Dalarnas familjehemsresurs (Dalarna Foster Care Resource)
coverage: Eleven municipalities: Avesta, Borlänge, Falun, Gagnef, Hedemora, Ludvika, Orsa, Rättvik, Säter, Vansbro and Älvdalen (hosted by Falun)
notes: Joint scheme that recruits, investigates and trains foster carers. The interest e-service needs BankID or Freja+; its steps are questions, family situation, preview and send. People can also book an information meeting, online or in person. A talk on carers' finances by SKR was listed for 10 December 2026.

name: Gävle kommun: Bli familjehem eller jourhem (Gävle Municipality: recruitment unit)
notes: The e-service needs an e-ID and says applicants must be at least 18. Its steps are applicant, family and housing, wishes, background and experience, then send. If the person goes further, the recruitment unit (Rekryteringsenheten) collects register extracts. Payment follows SKR. A carer who must stay at home can get an extra fee for lost earnings, backed by an employer's certificate.

name: Sundsvalls kommun: Bli familjehem (Sundsvall Municipality: become a foster carer)
notes: One e-service for several volunteer roles. Logging in is optional and only fills in contact details. Applicants must be over 18. A first call follows, and applicants consent to register extracts from the police, social services, Försäkringskassan and Kronofogden. Fostering page changed 18 November 2026.

name: Gemensam familjehemsorganisation Västernorrland (GFO, joint foster care organisation)
coverage: Six municipalities: Härnösand, Kramfors, Sollefteå, Timrå, Ånge and Örnsköldsvik
notes: The interest link leads to an e-service on Härnösand's site (not read). On the last Friday of each month people can book a one-to-one digital information meeting. The steps page says applicants order their own extracts from the police, Kronofogden, Transportstyrelsen (LOB register) and Försäkringskassan, to open together at the first home visit; then come the BRA-fam screening, references (one work and one private per adult), joint and individual interviews of 3 to 4 hours, and talks with any children. All training is free.

name: Familjehemscentrum Jämtlands län (Jämtland County Foster Care Centre)
coverage: Seven municipalities: Bräcke, Härjedalen, Krokom, Ragunda, Strömsund, Åre and Östersund (hosted by Östersund)
notes: Recruits, investigates and trains foster carers for the seven municipalities, and runs Ett hem att växa i for the carers it has assessed. The interest link leads to Östersund's e-service (not read). Östersund's own fostering page sends people here. Page updated 18 November 2026.

name: Umeå kommun: Familjehem (Umeå Municipality: foster care centre, Familjehemscentrum)
stated_response_time: As soon as we can, and within a week at the latest (senast inom en vecka)
notes: No login needed. The form asks for name, daytime phone, the best time to reach them, mobile, email, home town, other information and which roles interest them (foster home, emergency home, contact family, support family). People can also book a half-hour one-to-one digital information meeting (six times were offered on 27 November 2026). Form page updated 10 August 2026.

name: Skellefteå kommun: Familjehem och jourhem (Skellefteå Municipality: family home unit)
notes: No login, but the web form asks for full name and personal identity number (both required), children and their ages, address, phone, email, occupation, other information, roles of interest and how they heard. The FAQ says there is no age limit but carers should be over 25 (most are 30 to 60), and the child should have their own room. The unit avoids placing a child with the family's own children of about the same age.

name: Luleå kommun: Familjehem, kontaktfamilj, jourhem (Luleå Municipality: family home unit)
notes: The e-service page says the investigation takes 4 to 6 months and that Luleå aims to offer training before a placement. The investigation follows Socialstyrelsen's rules and its BRA-fam screening, with home visits, references and register extracts (police, Försäkringskassan, Kronofogden, the LOB register and social services). For emergency homes Luleå wants someone with experience or training with children, and no own children under 3.

name: Piteå kommun: Familjehem och jourfamiljehem (Piteå Municipality: foster and emergency care)
notes: E-service (not read). Piteå says carers can be aged 25 to 60 and need no formal qualification. The investigation includes visits at home and at the office, references and register extracts. Contracted foster homes can get extra pay for a carer at home part or full time for 6 months to 2 years.
